section: Minority rights - Articles 29 and 30, National Commission for Minorities, Sachar Committee, schemes
subsections: Sachar Committee - chair, year, mandate, Muslim groups, follow-ups

accepted.s: The Sachar Committee was set up in 2005 to examine which of the following?
o: The implementation of the linguistic reorganisation of States
The social, economic and educational status of Muslims in India
The status of internally displaced persons
The political representation of Scheduled Tribes
accepted.x: The Sachar Committee examined the social, economic and educational status of Muslims, including education, employment, income, credit and government jobs.
accepted.tq: Identify the mandate directly from the committee’s stated terms of reference.
accepted.sec: Sachar Committee - chair, year, mandate, Muslim groups, follow-ups  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Sachar Committee:
1. It was set up in 2005 by the Prime Minister.
2. It was chaired by Justice Rajinder Sachar.
3. Its report was submitted in November 2006.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The committee was set up in 2005, chaired by Justice Rajinder Sachar, and submitted its report in November 2006.
accepted.tq: Check the committee’s establishment, chair and report date separately before selecting the coded combination.
accepted.sec: Sachar Committee - chair, year, mandate, Muslim groups, follow-ups  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following was NOT specifically included among the areas examined by the Sachar Committee?
accepted.x: The committee examined education, employment, income, credit and government jobs. Judicial appointments were not among the listed areas of its mandate.
accepted.tq: Find the option outside the committee’s stated mandate.
accepted.sec: Sachar Committee - chair, year, mandate, Muslim groups, follow-ups  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
With reference to the Muslim social groups mentioned in the context of the Sachar Committee, consider the following statements:
1. Ashraf refers to groups associated with upper or claimed foreign origin.
2. Ajlaf refers to commoners and lower-caste converts.
3. Arzal refers to Dalit converts.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Ashraf, Ajlaf and Arzal are respectively associated with upper or claimed foreign origin, commoners or lower-caste converts, and Dalit converts.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the three closely related social classifications rather than relying on one familiar term.
accepted.sec: Sachar Committee - chair, year, mandate, Muslim groups, follow-ups  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which Muslim group was identified as requiring attention similar to that given to Hindu Other Backward Classes?
o: All Muslim groups equally under the same classification
accepted.x: The Ajlaf, described as backward Muslims or commoners and lower-caste converts, were identified as requiring attention similar to Hindu OBCs.
accepted.tq: Separate Ajlaf from Arzal by matching the group with the specific policy concern.
accepted.sec: Sachar Committee - chair, year, mandate, Muslim groups, follow-ups  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Ashraf — upper or claimed foreign origin
Ajlaf — the most deprived Dalit Muslim group
accepted.x: Arzal, rather than Ajlaf, was described as the Dalit Muslim group and the most deprived category. Ajlaf was identified as a backward group requiring attention similar to Hindu OBCs.
accepted.tq: Use the confusable-pair trap by checking the precise description of each group.
accepted.sec: Sachar Committee - chair, year, mandate, Muslim groups, follow-ups  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following was NOT a proposal associated with the Sachar Committee?
accepted.x: The Sachar Committee proposed an Equal Opportunity Commission, National Data Bank and Assessment and Monitoring Authority. A National Linguistic Minorities Commission was not listed among its proposals.
accepted.tq: Eliminate the option belonging to a different institutional theme.
accepted.sec: Sachar Committee - chair, year, mandate, Muslim groups, follow-ups  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Committee)
A. Sachar Committee
B. National Commission for Religious and Linguistic Minorities
C. Post-Sachar Evaluation Committee

List-II (Chair or key association)
1. Rajinder Sachar
2. Justice Ranganath Misra
3. Amitabh Kundu

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The Sachar Committee was chaired by Rajinder Sachar, the National Commission for Religious and Linguistic Minorities by Justice Ranganath Misra, and the Post-Sachar Evaluation Committee by Amitabh Kundu.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure chair-combination and eliminate codes containing a swapped committee.
accepted.sec: Sachar Committee - chair, year, mandate, Muslim groups, follow-ups  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following in chronological order of their reports or evaluation period:
A. Report of the Sachar Committee
B. Report of the National Commission for Religious and Linguistic Minorities
C. Post-Sachar Evaluation Committee period

Select the correct sequence.
accepted.x: The Sachar Committee report was submitted in 2006, the Ranganath Misra Commission report came in 2007, and the Kundu Committee evaluation related to 2013-14.
accepted.tq: Fix the earliest and latest entries first, then place the intervening report.
accepted.sec: Sachar Committee - chair, year, mandate, Muslim groups, follow-ups  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Ranganath Misra Commission was associated with which of the following recommendations?
o: Replacement of all State languages by Hindi
A 15% reservation and delinking Scheduled Caste status from religion
Creation of the National Data Bank for census purposes only
accepted.x: The National Commission for Religious and Linguistic Minorities, chaired by Justice Ranganath Misra, suggested a 15% quota for minorities and delinking SC status from religion.
accepted.tq: Match the commission with its distinctive recommendation rather than its general subject.
accepted.sec: Sachar Committee - chair, year, mandate, Muslim groups, follow-ups  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Kundu Committee, associated with the post-Sachar evaluation, was chaired by whom and related to which period?
accepted.x: The Post-Sachar Evaluation Committee was chaired by Prof. Amitabh Kundu and related to 2013-14. It reviewed the implementation of the Sachar recommendations.
accepted.tq: Use the chair-year combination to distinguish the follow-up committee from the original committee.
accepted.sec: Sachar Committee - chair, year, mandate, Muslim groups, follow-ups  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which scheme is primarily associated with leadership training for minority women?
accepted.x: Nai Roshni, launched in 2013, focuses on leadership training for minority women.
accepted.tq: Link the scheme’s name with its distinct beneficiary and purpose.

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Hamari Dharohar — preserving the heritage of minorities
Seekho aur Kamao — skill upgradation and placement
Nai Manzil — education and skilling for school dropouts
Nai Roshni — free coaching after clearing civil services preliminaries
accepted.x: Nai Roshni concerns leadership training for minority women. Free coaching and post-preliminary support are associated with Naya Savera and Nai Udaan.
accepted.tq: Reject the option that swaps the benefits of two neighbouring minority schemes.

accepted.s:
The PM’s New 15 Point Programme for the Welfare of Minorities is associated with which of the following objectives?
1. Education and a fair share in economic activity and jobs
2. Better living conditions
3. Prevention of communal violence
4. Earmarking of outlays for minorities

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The programme, introduced in 2006, covers education, economic activity and jobs, better living conditions, prevention of communal violence and earmarking of outlays for minorities.
accepted.tq: Treat each listed objective independently; the comprehensive combination is supported here.

accepted.s: Pre-matric and post-matric minority scholarships are provided through which platform using Direct Benefit Transfer?
accepted.x: The minority scholarships for the pre-matric and post-matric stages are provided through the National Scholarship Portal using DBT.
accepted.tq: Identify the delivery platform rather than confusing it with a committee proposal or loan institution.

accepted.s: The PM Jan Vikas Karyakram is best described as a scheme that:
o: Offers only leadership training to minority women
Provides only overseas scholarships to minority students
Provides loans exclusively to traditional artisans
Provides centrally sponsored infrastructure in minority-concentration areas for the benefit of all residents
accepted.x: PMJVK, introduced in May 2018, is a Centrally Sponsored infrastructure scheme in minority-concentration areas and benefits all residents of those areas.
accepted.tq: Apply the scheme’s beneficiary rule to distinguish area-based infrastructure from individual assistance.

accepted.s: PM Jan Vikas Karyakram was restructured from which earlier programme?
accepted.x: PMJVK was restructured from the Multi-sectoral Development Programme (MSDP), which dates from 2008-09.
accepted.tq: Use the predecessor-successor relationship to identify the correct programme.

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements regarding PM VIKAS is correct?
1. It stands for Pradhan Mantri Virasat Ka Samvardhan.
2. It is a Central Sector scheme introduced in 2022.
3. It merges five minority schemes.
4. It is intended to run until 2025-26.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: PM VIKAS means Pradhan Mantri Virasat Ka Samvardhan, was introduced in 2022 as a Central Sector scheme, merges five schemes and is intended to run until 2025-26.
accepted.tq: Verify the expansion, type, year, merger and duration before choosing the combination.

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT one of the five schemes merged into PM VIKAS?
accepted.x: PM VIKAS merges Seekho aur Kamao, USTTAD, Hamari Dharohar, Nai Roshni and Nai Manzil. PMJVK is not one of the five merged schemes.
accepted.tq: Find the area-based infrastructure scheme that does not belong to the merged skill and heritage package.

accepted.s: According to the stated design of PM VIKAS, which proportion of skilling seats is earmarked for women, and approximately how many beneficiaries are targeted?
accepted.x: PM VIKAS provides for 33% of skilling seats for women and is intended to benefit about 9 lakh persons.
accepted.tq: Match the two programme figures together; do not infer the percentage from the beneficiary count.

accepted.s: The post-matric scholarship for minorities is subject to which parental annual income ceiling?
accepted.x: The stated current income ceiling for the post-matric minority scholarship is parental income below ₹2.5 lakh.
accepted.tq: Prefer the specified current figure over the older competing figure of ₹2 lakh.

accepted.s: Which scheme provides free coaching or support to minority candidates after clearing UPSC, SSC and State PSC preliminary examinations?
accepted.x: Naya Savera provides free coaching, while Nai Udaan provides support after candidates clear the preliminary examinations of UPSC, SSC and State PSCs.
accepted.tq: Separate the coaching scheme from the post-preliminary support scheme within the paired names.

accepted.s: Which Article guarantees the right to submit a representation for redress of grievances in any language used in the Union or a State?
accepted.x: Article 350 provides the right to submit representations for the redress of grievances in any language used in the Union or in a State.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the general language-of-representation provision from the two linguistic-minority safeguards.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Article 350A concerns instruction in the mother tongue at the primary stage.
2. Article 350B provides for a Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities.
3. The Special Officer is appointed by the President.
4. Articles 350A and 350B were inserted by the Seventh Constitutional Amendment, 1956.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. Article 350A concerns mother-tongue instruction at the primary stage, Article 350B creates the Special Officer, and both provisions were inserted by the Seventh Amendment Act, 1956.
accepted.tq: Check the paired Articles, appointment authority and amendment year as separate constitutional details.

accepted.s: The Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities is required to:
o: Investigate and report on safeguards for linguistic minorities
Frame the language policy of every State
Decide disputes between State Governors and Chief Ministers
Appoint teachers for all primary schools
accepted.x: The Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities investigates and reports to the President on safeguards provided for linguistic minorities.
accepted.tq: Ask what the constitutional office actually does rather than assigning it a broader language-policy power.

accepted.s: In January 2026, concerns regarding Kannada speakers in Kasaragod were associated with which development?
o: A report of the Kundu Committee
A new Central Sector scholarship scheme
accepted.x: A language Bill in Kerala raised concerns for Kannada speakers in Kasaragod. Kerala stated that Clause 7 protected linguistic minorities.
accepted.tq: Link the reported concern to the State and legislative development, not to an older committee or constitutional amendment.
